notesStmt.note: The bottom portion of this page contains trial lines for "Sail Out for Good, Eidólon Yacht!," which was first published in the March 1891 issue of Lippincott's Magazine, along with a group of poems that were collectively titled "Old-Age Echoes." The poem was then included in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891). The title "Sail forth O mystic yacht of me" appears halfway down the page. The top portion of the page contains prose with no known connection to Whitman's published work, although the fact that it contains corrections suggests that Whitman was revising it for possible publication. On the verso Whitman wrote, twice, "Walt Whitman, July 30 1890." According to Horace Traubel, these were intended as autographs to be sent to admirers, but were never sent.
